scope: Independent full-passage review of three named nonmarket nodes, including every lifecycle-status entry, and their seven event classifications; targeted schema, references, display order and disconnected-node audit. Volume II, ch. XVIII §5, printed pp. 183–185 and p. 194

decisions.qualification: Procopius is a literary narrative; Bury relies on the same lineage. This classification does not establish the absence of transactions or govern every boat mill.

decisions.finding: Procopius reports working moored-boat mills; Bury places the aqueduct cuts and immediate response at the start of the 537–538 siege, supporting the stated year.

evidence.locator: ch. XVIII §5, printed pp. 183–185, 194

decisions.qualification: The precise bridge, degree of flour sufficiency, exact date and archaeological confirmation are not established by this review.

evidence.locator: First Ra voyage: 1969 Giza construction, Safi launch and expedition paragraphs

decisions.qualification: This is a mission-scoped classification and does not deny sponsorship, paid labor, media rights or transactions; a modern crossing does not prove ancient contact. The museum page internally conflicts: its body places construction at Giza but its Norwegian photo caption says Safi. The separately preserved contemporaneous photographer report supports the Giza region; the precise Giza pyramid is not part of the graph event.

verification.unit_tests: 72 tests passed on the current schema and validator.

repository_validation.limitation: Validation verifies the configured structure, references, review hashes and declared local-copy hashes; it does not independently prove each historical assertion.

verification.reviewed_ledger_membership: All 16 target node/event records match the ledger and current proposition hashes and review axes. All 37 molecular historical projections match current data.

limits: Inspected passages are not exhaustive readings of the surrounding books, newspapers or full dataset.
The reviewed nonmarket labels are scoped classifications/inferences, not proof of zero commercial transactions.
The PVS and museum histories have participant/institutional lineages; corroboration is not assumed independent when it is not.
Historical support and review-file integrity are separate questions. This review does not mutate data, grant a universal lifecycle acceptance or prove any alleged historical contact.
